title: Will AI make your degree pointless?
description:
AI isn’t just occasionally going rogue…(Open AI and Meta we’re looking at you) it’s also changing the world of work. Nearly 70% of college students in the US said they thought AI would make it harder to find a job in a recent survey - and 22% said that they’ve changed what they’re deciding to study at university because of this. They’re not the only ones… students all over the world are thinking about how to AI-proof their future careers.

In this episode, we go to the University College London campus to speak to three students: Omer, who’s studying French and German, Zahra, who’s studying entrepreneurship, and Allie, who’s just graduated from Kings College after completing her law studies. They tell us how they think AI could change the course of their careers, how they’re adapting to the new technology, and if their degrees will still be helpful in the face of AI.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討人工智慧 AI 對大學學位與未來職涯發展的影響。主持人 Hannah Gelbart 造訪倫敦大學學院 UCL 訪問三位學生與畢業生，探討他們如何看待 AI 帶來的威脅與機遇。主修語言的 Omer 表示，翻譯等文字工作雖易被 AI 取代，但人類面對面交流的情感與文化理解無法被複製；法律系畢業生 Allie 指出，律師事務所將 AI 視為需嚴格監督的初級助手，但也坦言缺乏傳統基礎工作鍛鍊恐影響職涯成長；主修創業學的 Zahra 則抱持樂觀態度，強調人機協同合作的重要性。受訪者一致認為大學學位的價值超越單純課業，並鼓勵學生結合 AI 工具，積極培養科技無法替代的人際溝通與實務技能。
summaryEn: Host Hannah Gelbart visits the University College London (UCL) campus to speak with three students and recent graduates—Omer (languages), Allie (law), and Zahra (entrepreneurship)—about how AI is impacting their studies and career prospects. Omer notes that while AI can easily handle written translation, human connection and cultural nuance remain irreplaceable. Allie discusses how law firms view legal AI as an error-prone junior assistant requiring supervision, though she worries about missing foundational entry-level tasks that help young professionals grow. Zahra takes an optimistic approach, advocating for human-led innovation working alongside AI. Overall, the guests agree that university degrees remain highly valuable for developing broader life skills and networking, advising prospective students to complement their passions with AI tools while focusing on uniquely human strengths.
